texts.facts: The present Detailed Accident Report arises out of road accident in which one Dan Singh (aged about 52 years) allegedly suffered grievous injury. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on intervening night of 12.04.2015 and 13.04.2015 at about 11:45 p.m. when petitioner along with one Ajay was crossing the red light near police station, Pul Prahladpur and moving towards Surajkund Road, a black colored Hero Splendor motor bike bearing Dan Singh vs Rajesh (17215 Ppp) on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179687555/ 1 no. DL-3SCW-4492 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle) came from Mehraulli side, driven at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and hit the petitioner. As an impact of the accident, petitioner was dragged on the road till a distance and sustained grievous injuries. Police was called. PCR vehicle arrived and took the petitioner to AIIMS Trauma Center. Driver of the offending vehicle was also apprehended. 3. An FIR no.172/15, dated 13.04.2015 was registered u/s 279,337 of IPC PS-Pul Prahladpur. Matter was investigated and a chargesheet u/s 279/338 of IPC and Section 3/118, 5/180 of MV Act was filed before concerned criminal court while DAR was Misc DJ no. 244/22 Dan Singh vs. Rajesh & ors. P.No. 2 of 22 ss filed before this Tribunal. 4. Respondent no.1 is the driver, respondent no.2 is the owner of the offending vehicle. Respondent no.3 is the insurer of the offending vehicle. 5. Respondent no.1 and 2 filed their reply denying the involvement of the offending vehicle or the occurrence of the accident. It has been pleaded that however, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding a valid and effective driving licence bearing no. UP5820120201591 issued by Licensing Authority, UP and a valid insurance policy bearing no. 39010231146202503885, valid from 19.10.2014 to 18.10.2015, issued by National Insurance Company. Respondent no.3/insurance company also filed its reply/written statement denying its liability to compensate the petitioner on the ground of breach of policy in as much as the driver of the offending vehicle did not have a valid driving licence and it is therefore that he had been chargesheeted u/s 3/181 MV Act also. Issuance of insurance policy as however not been denied. 6. Vide order dated 23.05.2025, following issues were framed. 1. Whether the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 12.04.2015 involving vehicle bearing no. DL-3SCW-4492 driven by R1 and owned by R2 and insured with R3 due to rash and negligent driving of R-1?OPP. 2. Whether the claimant is entitled to any compensation, if so, to what extent and from whom? OPP. 3. Relief. Misc DJ no. 244/22 Dan Singh vs. Rajesh & ors. P.No. 3 of 22 ss 7. In order to prove his claim, petitioner/injured Dan Singh led evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He deposed on the lines of the DAR. He stated that on 13.04.2015, he along with a relative Ajay, were going to Pul Prahladpur. At about 11:45 p.m, when they were crossing the MB Road towards Surajkund, a vehicle bearing no.DL-3SCE-4492 came from Mehruali side driven by respondent no.1 in a rash and negligent manner and hit the victim. Due to the impact, he fell on the road and sustained injuries. A PCR call was made by unknown person and victim was taken to AIIMS Trauma Center. Dan Singh vs Rajesh (17215 Ppp) on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179687555/ 2 PW-1 further deposed that he was working as a bus driver and earning of Rs.25,000/- per month. PW-1 relied upon documents i.e. DAR as Ex.PW1/1, Medical documents as Ex.PW1/2, Adhar card and PAN card as Ex.PW1/3 and driving licence as Ex.PW1/4. PW-1 was duly cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company/respondent no.3. 8. Respondent no.1 and 2 did not lead evidence despite opportunity. Respondent no.3 led evidence by examining Sh. Vineet Kumar, Assistant Manager, National Insurance company as R3W1. He tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.R3W1/A. R3W1 relied upon Notice u/O 12 Rule 8 of CPC as Ex.R3W1/1, Two speed post dated 28.07.2025 as Ex.R3W1/2 and Ex.R3W1/3, two tracking report as Ex.R3W1/4 and Ex.R3W1/5, insurance policy as Ex.R3W1/6 and complete DAR as Ex.R3W1/7. Misc DJ no. 244/22 Dan Singh vs. Rajesh & ors. P.No. 4 of 22 ss R3W1 was not cross examined by any of the respondents. the injured suffered injuries in a road traffic accident dated 12.04.2015 involving vehicle bearing no. DL-3SCW-4492 driven by R1 and owned by R2 and insured with R3 due to rash and negligent driving of R-1?OPP. 10. 11. In the present case, petitioner examined himself to prove the factum and occurrence of the accident. As PW-1, petitioner has testified on the lines of the DAR and deposed that the accident occurred while he was crossing the red light. He has categorically alleged rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle. The offending vehicle was seized from the spot and the driver /respondent no.1 was apprehended by the police on the same date. Accordingly, issue no.1 is decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents. . In the instant case insurance company/respondent no. 3 has raised statutory defence as to breach of terms of the insurance policy alleging that the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 without a valid driving licence.
texts.arguments: Reliance is placed upon decision in Bimla Devi & ors. vs. Himachal Road Transport Corporation & Ors. (2009) 13 SC 535, in Parmeshwari vs. Amir Chand & Ors., 2011 (1) SCR 1096 and National Insurance Company Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana, 2009 ACJ 287, wherein it has been held that the negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view has to be taken. In National Insurance Co. vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 13. It may further be noted that in Cholamandalam Insurance Company vs. Kamlesh, 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if the driver of the offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an adverse inference can be drawn against him. As regards the quantum of compensation, this court is governed by the law laid down by Hon'le Supreme Court in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343, Sarla Verma & Ors. v. Delhi Transport Corporation & Ors. (2003) 6SCC 121 and National Insurance Company Limited v. Pranay Sethi & Ors.(2017) 16 SCC 680. The gist of the law is that the object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 17. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and Misc DJ no. 244/22 Dan Singh vs. Rajesh & ors. P.No. 8 of 22 ss miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 17.1. 17.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), Dan Singh vs Rajesh (17215 Ppp) on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179687555/ 5 (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 17.4. Award under the head of future medical expenses--Item Misc DJ no. 244/22 Dan Singh vs. Rajesh & ors. P.No. 9 of 22 ss (iii)--depends upon specific medical evidence regarding need for further treatment and cost thereof. 17.6. Observation of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Rajkumar v. Ajay Kumar & Anr. is quoted hereunder: "10. Ascertainment of the effect of the permanent disability on the actual earning capacity involves three steps. On the other hand, if the claimant was a clerk in government service, the loss of his left hand may not result in loss of employment and he may still be continued as a clerk as he could perform his clerical functions; and in Misc DJ no. 244/22 Dan Singh vs. Rajesh & ors. P.No. 10 of 22 ss that event the loss of earning capacity will not be 100% as in the case of a driver or carpenter, nor 60% which is the actual physical disability, but far less. Vs. Jaibir Singh & Ors whereby the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi has formulated MACAD(Motor Accident Claims Annunity Deposit Scheme) which has been made effective from 01.01.2019. The State Bank of India, Saket Courts, Delhi is directed to disburse the amount in accordance with MACAD formulated by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi. 29. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". Moreover, in the case of literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view Dan Singh vs Rajesh (17215 Ppp) on 17 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/179687555/ 11 to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit.
